_note: Policy file -- global registry of TRACKED-THREAD root identity only (phase-0.6-plan.md §A6) -- a root is a hand-curated set of Strong's/lemma ids (joshua_study_style_reference.md §2), not a string, not a translit/gloss/colour bundle. Local (non-thread) roots stay in a unit's own unit-meta roots[] {root, translit, gloss} and are counted per-verse; they don't belong here. Shape is deliberately flat and minimal: {ids, note} only -- no kind/members (Matthew built and reverted that taxonomy the same day it shipped), no translit/gloss/colour (those live with the thread's other data, not with its id-set). Every id here must exist as a lemma in Joshua-words.tsv and must belong to exactly one root (pipeline/roots.py enforces both, plus that every threads.json thread's `root` resolves to an entry here). Promotion policy (2026-09-16, Lane): Claude decides which of a unit's thread candidates go book-wide vs. stay local, biased toward book-wide -- a thread kept local when a real payoff shows up later is worse than one tracked and never paying off. Claude asks Lane only when genuinely unsure (e.g. a root so frequent -- kol -- that tracking it would carry no signal).

give.note: natan, Qal give. ×8 in unit 1's speeches (participle 'is giving' vs. perfect 'gave/have given' -- the land as gift, already done and not yet done); central to the book's land-as-gift theology.

cross.note: ʿavar (verb, cross over) + ʿever (noun, the far side) -- one root, both ids. The book's first command (qum ʿavor, 1:2); the Jordan crossing is unit 3's whole subject.

possess.note: yarash, Qal possess. Only the Qal occurs in unit 1; the Hiphil 'drive out' (same root family) arrives later in the conquest narrative -- tracked so the stem split is visible when it does.

inherit.note: naḥal-Hiphil (tanḥil, 'cause to inherit,' 1:6) + naḥalah (the noun 'inheritance'), merged up front -- naḥalah is the load-bearing word of the whole allotment movement (units 13-20).

rest.note: nuaḥ, Hiphil give rest. Only 3 occurrences in unit 1 but explicitly sets up the book's completion formula, restated at 21:44, 22:4, 23:1 -- small count, high thematic payoff.

strong.note: ḥazaq, be strong. The 'be strong and be firm' refrain recurs at 10:25 and elsewhere; paired throughout with 'firm' (ʾamats).

firm.note: ʾamats, be firm/resolute. Always paired with ḥazaq in this unit; kept as its own root per the colour-pairing policy rather than merged into 'strong'.

torah.note: torah, 'the scroll of the torah' (1:8). Opens a line to 8:31-34, 22:5, and 23:6.

servant.note: ʿeved, servant. Moses' title ('servant of Yahweh') throughout unit 1 -- watch whether and when Joshua receives the same title (24:29).

send.note: shalaḥ, send. 'Wherever you send us we will go' (1:16) is answered immediately: 2:1 opens with Joshua sending the spies.

devote.note: ḥaram, Hiphil devote to destruction. First occurrence in the book is in Rahab's mouth (2:10), before Israel has devoted a single city -- becomes the governing law of the conquest (Jericho, Ai, and the campaign reports).

swear.note: shavaʿ̲ (Niphal swear) + shevuʿ̲ah (the noun, oath) -- one root, both ids. Yahweh's oath to the fathers (1:6, retro'd from unit 1) opens it; Rahab's oath (2:12, 17, 20) is the first oath sworn between people in the book, kept at 6:22; the Gibeonite oath (9:15, 19-20) and the rest formula (21:43-44) carry it to the end.

blood.note: dam, blood. 'His blood on his head' (2:19) is the bloodguilt logic the cities-of-refuge law runs on -- the blood-avenger of 20:3, 5, 9.

melt.note: masas, Niphal melt. Rahab's 'our heart melted' (2:11) returns for the Amorite and Canaanite kings (5:1) and, reversed, for Israel after Ai (7:5).

all.why: kol, 236 occurrences book-wide. Asked Lane (the frequency made it a genuine toss-up) and kept local: a root that common carries no signal as a tracked thread -- colouring it would tint the page without telling a reader anything. Re-propose only with a specific payoff in view, not on frequency alone.

cross-fords.why: maʿ̲berot, 'the fords' (2:7) -- cognate with the tracked 'cross' root but a distinct lemma (4569b) and a single occurrence. Widening an already-tracked thread's id set on one thin hit isn't the same call as promoting a new one; declined for now. Re-propose only if maʿ̲berot recurs with its own payoff.
